A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same importance-based token-merging work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative and qualitative experiments on text-to-image, multi-view, and video generation, including method ablations and supplementary pruning and sampling-step studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds PixArt-α, consistency-model, cross-attention, token-importance, and acceleration-combination experiments.

M1.justification: The core important-token pool, destination sampling, and partitioning procedure remain. v2 adds an implemented cross-attention-based importance variant and uses pixel-location distance instead of feature similarity for PixArt-α matching (Section 4.3 and Appendix B). The original early-pruning procedure is retained in Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions cover text-to-image, image-conditioned multi-view, and text-to-video generation, retaining MS-COCO, GSO, and VBench evaluations. PixArt-α, consistency models, and acceleration combinations expand model configurations without establishing new datasets, task requirements, or input environments.

E2.justification: v2 adds ToFu to the Stable Diffusion quantitative and qualitative comparisons (Table 1 and Figures 5 and 9). It also adds unmerged Zero123++ outputs to the supplementary multi-view comparison (Figure 11). ToMeSD and the qualitative ATC comparison remain.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluation configurations: PixArt-α uses 20 sampling steps, CFG 4.5, and merging in self- and cross-attention layers 7–20; Appendix A adds a four-step consistency model, controlled top/bottom-30% pruning, and acceleration combinations. The design ablation also replaces r=0.6 with r=0.7. Original Stable Diffusion, Zero123++, and AnimateDiff settings are largely retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of cross-attention importance, whether high-CFG tokens matter more than low-CFG tokens, compatibility with DeepCache/Faster Diffusion/FRDiff, and sensitivity to pruning duration across three tasks (Tables 8, 10, 12, and 15). The original early-pruning and sampling-step analyses remain as Tables 14 and 13.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The additional v2 tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive quantitative and qualitative results for ToFu, PixArt-α, cross-attention, consistency models, and supplementary analyses. For example, its new PixArt-α comparison reports FID 34.02 versus ToMeSD’s 65.46 at r=0.5. Within retained multi-view settings, the proposed method’s r=0.6 PSNR changes from 14.83 to 14.85 and LPIPS from 0.269 to 0.263 (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 3). The changed design-ablation rows use different merging ratios, rather than demonstrate same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 2 adds the approximate relationship between CFG magnitude and the conditional log-likelihood gradient. It also corrects the ablation discussion’s pool-size expression from (1+r)(1+p) to (1−r)(1+p), matching the formula already used in v1’s method. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claim that preserving important tokens improves generation quality at comparable computational cost remains. v2 broadens the contribution framing from CFG-based selection to a framework accepting different importance signals and explicitly extends its performance claims across U-Net and transformer architectures.

C2.justification: v2 adds a gradient-based saliency interpretation of CFG and revises the step-distilled-model limitation by explaining and demonstrating an attention-map workaround. It acknowledges the alternative’s possible memory cost and suggests weighted importance signals for multi-guidance scenarios. The existing warning about temporal merging reducing video dynamics remains.

D1.justification: v2 supplies implementation information for the extensions, including PixArt-α layer placement, sampling settings and spatial matching, final-block attention-map averaging, and the LCM Dreamshaper v7 configuration. It also supplies new qualitative prompts. Most original sampling, pruning, hardware, and metric-library details remain, with several moved into Appendix B.

R1.justification: v2 adds five cited works, including InstructPix2Pix, Faster Diffusion, ToMA, and LCM-LoRA, while retaining the earlier references. ToFu was already cited in v1 but receives an explicit methodological contrast in v2. Architectural background expands without substantially reorganizing the related-work positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around general importance-based merging. The standalone preliminaries section is removed and its relevant explanations integrated elsewhere. Early-pruning discussion and several implementation settings move to the appendix, substantially revising the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the examples in Figures 1 and 4, transposes and expands Figure 5 to include ToFu, and adds PixArt-α visual comparisons. Table 1 gains comparator columns, several new experimental tables appear, and supplementary image grids expand to include additional method variants and unmerged Zero123++ outputs.

improvement.justification: v1’s broad applicability claim rested on related U-Net-based models and left step-distilled models as a limitation. v2 materially strengthens that evidence through PixArt-α and attention-based consistency-model experiments, a relevant ToFu comparison, and a direct test of CFG token importance (Tables 2, 11, 1, and 10). These additions address important generalization and mechanism-validation gaps. Cross-attention has a stated memory tradeoff and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but the overall evidential basis is substantially stronger.
